summary: MVP safety invariants are carried forward as Runtime Foundation entry and exit gates, with new runtime-specific scenarios for model output, observations, memory, approvals, and recovery.

acceptance.evidence: runtime-safety-gates.md keeps the existing safety.rs scenario list mandatory for every runtime wave.

acceptance.criterion: New runtime tasks cannot be completed if they bypass semantic tools, policy, audit, or rollback.
acceptance.evidence: runtime-safety-gates.md defines completion rules that block direct model-to-tool, planner-to-shell, SecurityExecutionEngine bypass, and duplicate safety stacks.

acceptance.criterion: Secret, memory, and observation-specific risks have explicit regression fixtures.
acceptance.evidence: runtime-safety-gates.md defines observation-injection, observation-secret-redaction, memory-poisoning-policy-override, and memory-secret-retention runtime scenarios.

acceptance.criterion: Release readiness requires both old MVP safety gates and new AgentCore gates.
acceptance.evidence: runtime-safety-gates.md wave regression table requires MVP tests plus AgentCore, safety, and release checks for later waves.
